articles.title: 'Money-grab' or celebration? NFL kicks off London series
articles.standfirst: The NFL kicked off this season's series of London games on Sunday but the build-up was overshadowed by anger from long-term fans over ticket prices.

gist: Thousands of tickets remained available for some NFL London games due to slow sales.
Fans criticised steep price hikes and the scrapping of discounted season-ticket packages.
Despite complaints, the games continue to attract large crowds and celebrity attendees.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The NFL kicked off its London series with a game between the Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts. Although one upcoming fixture sold out quickly, thousands of tickets were initially left unsold, prompting the NFL to drop prices and offer discounted or free tickets.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Long-term supporters felt priced out by ticket increases that exceeded inflation and the removal of season-ticket packages. Some fans viewed the changes as a money-grab that alienated loyal attendees in favour of newer consumers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The NFL continues its international series with upcoming matches in London, featuring teams such as the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars.

sections.heading: Why it matters
